newsitem.title: GERMANY: Italy no longer needs weak currency, official says.
newsitem.headline: Italy no longer needs weak currency, official says.

text.p: Italy no longer needs to fall back on currency devaluations as a policy tool because inflationary pressures have receded recently, a senior Italian government official said on Tuesday.

"We are committed to stability, and entering the currency union will force economic policy of nations to use different instruments," Dino Piero Giarda, undersecretary of Italy's Ministry of Treasury and Budget said during an international video conference.

Noting that Italy had in past years resorted to devaluing its currency because very high inflation rates had chipped away at Italy's competitive advantages, Giarda said "there is a substitute to devaluation," now.

Italy's efforts to curb inflation rates have allowed Italy to give up these earlier used policies, Giarda assured, when told that Italy would no longer be able to resort to these methods once a member of Europe's currency union.
Giarda was participating in Global 24, a conference on European monetary union.
